title: GDLLM Now Supports Your ChatGPT Subscriptions!
author: Exonfang
selftext:
The most common request I have received since launching GDLLM, the fully transparent in-editor agentic harness for Godot, was to add the ability to use your ChatGPT subscription directly with the harness.

I am pleased to release version 1.5.0 which adds this functionality. Since 1.0.0, I've also improved the initial setup process, added a very nice to look at condensed feed toggle, and fixed a few bugs; so if you're on an older version, I strongly encourage you to update!

And of course, you can still connect to any other provider, local or cloud, via API directly! Now supporting both the Chat Completions and Responses API.

As you can tell from my release history and activity in issues, I am committed to actively developing this addon, for the benefit of the Godot community. 

Please let me know if there are any other features you'd like support for.

comments.author: Minimum_Hour519
comments.body: how does it compare to moshcode cli?

replies.author: Exonfang
replies.body:
Moshcode CLI just drives an existing, general harness like Codex, Claude, or Opencode.

General harnesses are great when it comes to general software engineering, but they fall short when it comes to very specific tasks.

I put a lot of work (and hundreds of millions of tokens in ablation testing) into GDLLM to refine its toolset to complete Godot tasks in less turns, more reliably, and with fewer tokens.

A lot of this is achieved by a lot of specific handling built into the harness to improve models working within Godot specifically. For example, there's uid handling, tooling around any data that isn't easy for a model to read or write (e.g. anything that's saved as a binary, or to reduce extremely verbose outputs into less verbose outputs that preserve all relevant data), allowing the agent to hook directly into a running game, all outputs, performance monitors, etc.

MCP servers also provide a lot of this tooling, but they suffer from all of the bloat of also including the general harness handling/tooling/system message, which brings GDLLM alone farther ahead of even a general harness plus a Godot specific MCP server.

replies.author: AguilaAurea
replies.body: Osea, lo que entiendo, es q mejora el flujo de trabajo entre Godot y la IA. O entendí mal?

replies.author: Exonfang
replies.body:
Correct - you can ask it do anything in Godot and it gives the model the ability to actually complete that work.

Basically, it's the Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, or Google Antigravity, but very specific for Godot. There are a lot of advantages for using a more application specific harness over a general one.

replies.author: LocoMod
replies.body:
GDLLM is just a Godot plugin that lets you invoke AI from inside the Godot editor with some basic LLM tools and a few other things. It's really more for the convenience of chatting with LLM inside Godot editor. If you are developing games with Godot and LLM, I would use Codex or Claude Code and prompt them to use Godot CLI and point them at the Godot project you created. There is also Godot MCP servers you can add to those.

An actual "harness" is more advanced than the standard AI loop most people are using by default. The word is just being used in the wrong context most of the time. A "harness" is when the entire LLM stack is specifically configured for specific use case like game development. You usually have to go beyond the default configurations in apps like Codex, Claude Code and GDLLM for it to actually be a "harness". It is everything that you have customized to maximize the utility of LLM for some purpose like research, or game development, etc.

replies.author: Exonfang
replies.body:
I encourage you to check out the repo! GDLLM is a legitimate harness with a robust feature set and goes significantly above what Opencode does, narrowed down specifically for Godot.

It is **significantly more** than a simple loop that allows you to invoke AI within the editor.

\> A "harness" is when the entire LLM stack is specifically configured for specific use case like game development. ... It is everything that you have customized to maximize the utility of LLM for some purpose like research, or game development, etc.

This is exactly what GDLLM is doing. By focusing solely on Godot game development, it actually outperforms Opencode even combined with a Godot specific MCP.
